chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Musa ibn Umar from Mu'ammara ibn Khallad said:

Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) sent for me regarding a need, so I entered upon him and he said, 'Return, and when it is tomorrow, come, and do not come except after the sunrise, for I sleep after praying Fajr.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This narration came as a concession (rukhsah), and it is preferable that a person not sleep after Fajr until sunrise, and it is permissible that the Imam (peace be upon him) only slept due to an excuse he had.

key_terms.رُخْصَةً: a concession or dispensation from a general rule

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sleeping after the Fajr prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the distinction between the Imam’s voluntary concession (*rukhsah*) and the recommended practice (*mustahabb*) for the general faithful to remain awake after Fajr for dhikr and reflection. Scholars note that while the Imam slept due to a specific reason, the ideal spiritual state involves utilizing the early morning hours for worship before the sun rises, a practice deeply rooted in the concept of *Barakah* in the dawn hours.
